raw_response:
Let me think through this as the farmer.

---

*I've been farming this land since before most of these young extension people were born. Six mu — I know every corner of it. Cotton on one side, maize on the other. My son and daughter-in-law are in the city most of the year, my wife helps when she can, the grandchildren are in school. It's mostly me.*

*I'm getting old. My back doesn't let me do what I used to. Picking cotton three times over September and October — that's the hardest part. Used to do it all myself. Now I do 2 mu cotton, not more. The other 4 mu I put in maize. Maize I can mostly hire a machine for planting. Cotton I have to nurse along myself.*

*For cotton, I put in one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. Same as always. When it flowers and starts setting bolls, I'll sprinkle some urea — maybe half a small bag per mu. That's what my neighbor Old Zhang does and his cotton always looks better than mine when he does it. Water twice: once when I transplant the seedlings if it's dry, once during boll-setting if there's no rain. For bugs — the bollworm always comes, I know to spray in July and August. I buy whatever the agrochemical shop has.*

*For maize, I hire a machine now to plant. My legs aren't what they were. One bag of compound per mu as base, put it in the furrow before the machine comes. When it's knee-high I come back and scatter some urea by hand — about 10 jin per mu, I eyeball it. One or two waterings if the summer is dry like last year. It usually rains enough in July and August but if it doesn't I run the pump.*

*This year the fertilizer shop said prices went up again. I'll use a little less on the maize — it's more forgiving than cotton. Cotton I won't cut corners on. The cotton is what I sell for cash.*
